title: Venezuela
subtitle: or, Sketches of Life in a South-American Republic; with the History of the Loan of 1864

summary: In 1864 Edward B. Eastwick, a former British diplomat in Persia, went to Venezuela as commissioner for the Venezuelan loan of that year. The first twelve chapters tell of the voyage by the Royal Mail steamer through St. Thomas to La Guaira, of Caracas and its bells, earthquake, and cemetery, of a bull-fight, of ministers and their breakfasts, and of journeys by Puerto Cabello to Valencia, to the battlefield of Carabobo, to the camp of President Falcon, and through the coffee valleys of Aragua. Two further chapters set out the resources of the country and the history of its debts to England. The appendix, about seventy pages, prints the loan contract, prospectuses and decrees, an exhibition catalogue, an account of the gold mines of the Yuruari, the constitution of 1864, and the accounts of the loan.
notes_on_text: The map announced on the title page is not in the copy scanned for this edition, nor in the two other copies at the Internet Archive; it is missing here.
The contents of this edition give each chapter a short title of the editor’s, taken from the opening words of its summary, and each appendix a short description; the summaries follow in full.
The book’s errata list (“for Engelckye, read Engelke”, pp. 126–128) is applied in the text, each place marked as a correction.
A letter printed within a footnote on p. 336 (from New Court, 10th July, 1865) is given as one paragraph of the note; its line breaks are not kept.
